en: Saṁyutta Nikāya 43.1 (SN 43.1, PTS SN iv 359) 1.
First Chapter: Mindfulness Directed to the Body (Kāyagatāsati Sutta)
At Sāvatthī.
"Monks, I will teach you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Listen to that."
And what, monks, is the unconditioned? That which, monks,
is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—
this, monks, is called the unconditioned.
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Mindfulness directed to the body.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned.
“Thus, monks, has the unconditioned been taught to you by me, and the path leading to the unconditioned has been taught.
Whatever, monks, ought to be done by a Teacher who seeks the welfare of his disciples and is compassionate, out of compassion—that has been done for you by me.
Here, monks, are the roots of trees; here are empty huts. Meditate, monks, do not be negligent; do not later fall into regret. This is my instruction to you.”

First Chapter
The Discourse on the Factors of Enlightenment:

The seven factors of enlightenment. This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned …” [as above].
The Tenth.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 43.11 (SN 43.11, PTS SN iv 361) 1.
First Chapter
The Discourse on the Factors of the Path: “And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
It is the noble eightfold path.”
"This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned.
Thus, monks, the unconditioned has been taught to you by me, and the path leading to the unconditioned has been taught.
Whatever was to be done by a Teacher who seeks the welfare of his disciples and is compassionate, out of compassion, that has been done for you by me."
“Bhikkhus, these are the roots of trees, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent; do not later fall into regret. This is my instruction to you.
The eleventh.
The first chapter of the Connected Discourses on the Unconditioned.
Its summary verse:
The body, serenity, with applied thought,
emptiness, and the foundations of mindfulness.
The right efforts, the bases of psychic power,
the faculties, the powers, and the factors of enlightenment; with the Path as the eleventh, [these constitute the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment].
Its summary is now recited.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 43.12 (SN 43.12, PTS SN iv 362) 2.
Second Chapter (Dutiyavagga)
The Unconditioned Discourse:
“Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Listen to that.”
And what, monks, is the unconditioned? That which, monks,
is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—
this, monks, is called the unconditioned.
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Serenity.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned.
"Thus, monks, has the unconditioned been taught by me to you, and the path leading to the unconditioned has been taught.
Whatever, monks, should be done by a Teacher who seeks the welfare of his disciples and is compassionate, out of compassion, that has been done for you by me.
Here, monks, are the roots of trees; here are empty huts. Meditate, monks, do not be negligent; do not later fall into regret. This is our instruction to you."
"And I will teach you, monks, the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Listen to that.
And what, monks, is the unconditioned?"
“Monks, that which is the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion—
this, monks, is called the unconditioned.
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?”
Vipassanā.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned.
Thus, monks, has the unconditioned been taught by me to you... [as before] ...pe... [as before] ...pe... [as before].
"This is our instruction to you. And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
It is concentration accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought.
"This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Concentration that is without applied thought and with sustained thought."
"This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Concentration without applied thought and without sustained thought. This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned..."
"And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
It is emptiness concentration.
This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned..."
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Signless concentration.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned... [as before] ...
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
It is the desireless concentration. This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
What, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
"Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world.
This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"
"Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating feelings in feelings … [as before] … This, monks,
is called the path leading to the unconditioned … And what,
monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"
"Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the mind in the mind...
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"
"Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating phenomena in phenomena... This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
What, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states, a monk generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives."
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the abandoning of evil, unwholesome states that have arisen.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, for the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen, a monk generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives.
“Monks, this is called the path leading to the unconditioned … And what,
monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk dwells for the stability, non-confusion, and further increase of wholesome states that have arisen.”
He generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for its expansion, development, and fulfillment. This, monks,
is called the path leading to the unconditioned… What,
monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
"Here, monks, a monk develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration through desire and volitional formations of striving.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"
"Here, monks, a monk develops the basis for psychic power endowed with energy and the volitional formations of striving.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"
"Here, monks, a monk develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving.
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?"

"Here, monks, a monk develops the basis for psychic power endowed with the concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving. This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
What, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of faith, dependent on seclusion, dependent on dispassion, dependent on cessation, resulting in relinquishment."
"This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of energy, based on seclusion... [as before]..."
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned … And what,
monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of mindfulness … [as before] …”
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of concentration... [as before]...
“Monks, this is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?

Here, monks, a monk develops the faculty of wisdom, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...”
"And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the power of faith, based on seclusion...
[as before] ...this, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned... [as before]"
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the power of energy … [as before] … This, bhikkhus,
is called the path leading to the unconditioned … [as before] …
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, monks, a monk develops the power of mindfulness … [as before] … This, monks,
is called the path leading to the unconditioned … [as before] …
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the power of concentration … [as before] … This, bhikkhus,
is called the path leading to the unconditioned … [as before] …
And what, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?

Here, monks, a monk develops the power of wisdom, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
What, monks, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
“Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness, based on seclusion...
This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned...
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?”
Here, monks, a bhikkhu develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena …pe… he develops the enlightenment factor of energy …pe… he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture …pe…
He develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility …pe… he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration …pe… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity,
which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment. This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned …pe….
"And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right view, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
This, bhikkhus, is called the path leading to the unconditioned... [and so forth].
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right intention … right speech … [and so on] … right livelihood.
He develops right action … [and so on] … he develops right livelihood … [and so on] … he develops right effort … [and so on] …
He develops right mindfulness...
"And, monks, I will teach you the unconditioned and the path leading to the unconditioned.
Listen to that."
"And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned …pe…?
And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the unconditioned?
Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops right concentration, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment."
This, monks, is called the path leading to the unconditioned.
Thus, monks, the unconditioned has been taught to you by me, and the path leading to the unconditioned has been taught.
Whatever was to be done by a teacher who seeks the welfare of his disciples and is compassionate, out of compassion, that has been done for you by me.
“Bhikkhus, these are the roots of trees, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent; do not later fall into regret. This is our instruction to you.
Thus was the first [discourse]. *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 43.13.
2. The Second Chapter:
The Discourse on the Unprotected “Monks, I will teach you the unprotected and the path leading to the unprotected.”
Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the unconditioned? ...
[It should be expanded in the same way as the unconditioned.]
The Second [Discourse].
Saṃyutta Nikāya 43.14–43 (SN 43.14, PTS SN iv 369) 2.
The Second Chapter (Dutiyavagga)
The Discourse on the Untainted, etc.
“Monks, I will teach you the untainted and the path leading to the untainted.
Listen to that. And what, monks, is the untainted? …”
“Monks, I will teach you truth and the path leading to truth.
Listen to that. And what, monks, is truth?
… [as above] … Monks, I will teach you the further shore and the path leading to the further shore.”
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the further shore?

... Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the subtle? ... Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the path leading to the subtle? ... Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the subtle? ... [and so on].
“Monks, I shall teach you that which is very difficult to see and the path leading to that which is very difficult to see.
Listen to that. And what, monks, is that which is very difficult to see?
… [as above] … And I shall teach you, monks, that which is ageless and the path leading to that which is ageless.”
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the undecaying? ... [as above] ...
And, bhikkhus, I will teach you the permanent and the path leading to the permanent.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the permanent? ... [as above] ...

Listen to that. And what, monks, is the ‘looked-at’?
… [as above] … And what, monks, is the ‘invisible’ and the path leading to the invisible?”
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the non-manifest...
[as above] ...And, bhikkhus, I will teach you the non-proliferated and the path leading to the non-proliferated.
Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the state free from proliferation (*nippapañca*)?
… [as before] … I will teach you, bhikkhus, the peaceful (*santa*) and the path leading to the peaceful.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the peaceful? … [as before] …
“Monks, I will teach you the Deathless and the path leading to the Deathless.
Listen to that. And what, monks, is the Deathless?
… [as above] … And what, monks, is the sublime and the path leading to the sublime?”
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the sublime?
… [as before] … And, bhikkhus, I shall teach you the auspicious and the path leading to the auspicious.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the auspicious? … [as before] …”
"And I shall teach you, bhikkhus, security and the path leading to security.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is security...
[as before] ...And I shall teach you, bhikkhus, the destruction of craving and the path leading to the destruction of craving."
Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the destruction of craving? ...
Bhikkhus, I will teach you the wonderful and the path leading to the wonderful.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the wonderful? ... [as above] ...
And I shall teach you, bhikkhus, the marvelous and the path leading to the marvelous.
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the marvelous? ... [as above] ...

Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the state free from calamity?

Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the shelter? … [as above] …
“Monks, I will teach you refuge and the path leading to refuge.
Listen to that. And what, monks, is refuge? … [as above] … And I will teach you, monks, protection and the path leading to protection.”
Listen to that. And what, bhikkhus, is the refuge? ... [as above] ...
The thirty-second.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 43.44 (SN 43.44, PTS SN iv 373)
2. Second Chapter:
The Discourse on the Ultimate Goal “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the ultimate goal and the path leading to the ultimate goal.”
Listen to that.
And what, bhikkhus, is the ultimate goal?
It is, bhikkhus, the destruction of lust, the destruction of hatred, and the destruction of delusion.
This, monks, is called the ultimate resort.
And what, monks, is the path leading to that ultimate resort?
It is mindfulness directed to the body (kāyagatāsati).
"This, monks, is called the path leading to the further shore.
Thus, monks, the further shore has been taught to you by me, and the path leading to the further shore has been taught.
Whatever was to be done by a Teacher who seeks the welfare of his disciples and is compassionate, out of compassion, that has been done for you by me."
“Bhikkhus, these are the roots of trees, these are empty huts. Meditate, bhikkhus, do not be negligent; do not later fall into regret. This is our instruction to you.
(This should be expanded in the same manner as the Unconditioned [Sutta].
Thirty-third.
The Second Chapter.
Its summary (uddāna) is:
The unconditioned, the undecaying, the taintless;
And truth, which is the further shore, subtle and very difficult to see;
undecaying, stable, and clearly perceived;
non-manifest, free from proliferation, and peaceful.
The deathless, sublime, auspicious, and secure;
the destruction of craving, wonderful and marvelous;
free from affliction, possessing a nature free from affliction.
This is Nibbāna, taught by the Sugata:
freedom from affliction, dispassion, purity, liberation, and non-attachment.
"It is an island, a shelter,
a protection, and a refuge.
The Connected Discourses on the Unconditioned are complete.
